subtopic: The cell's energy powerhouses and their surprising origins
narrative_arc: hook → definition → process → scale → surprise → consequence → summary

concepts.definition: Organelles converting glucose and oxygen into ATP for cellular energy.
The energy currency fueling nearly every cellular process in the body.
Mitochondria were once free-living bacteria, now permanent cell residents.
Dysfunction leads to severe health issues like muscle weakness and neurodegeneration.

story_beats.speaker_cue: Mitochondria are often called the powerhouses of the cell.
They convert glucose and oxygen into ATP, the energy currency that fuels nearly every cellular process.
The glucose and oxygen you absorbed ten seconds ago are already being processed.

story_beats.intent: Quantify the immense scale of energy output
story_beats.speaker_cue: Every minute, your body produces roughly 9 × 10^20 ATP molecules...
Each mitochondrion has its own DNA, hinting they were once free-living bacteria.

story_beats.intent: Warn of the severe impact of their failure
story_beats.speaker_cue: When mitochondria fail, the consequences are catastrophic: muscle weakness, neurodegeneration, even death.
Understanding them is understanding life itself.

key_takeaways: Mitochondria are the essential powerhouses, converting fuel into energy for all life.
Your body produces an astonishing 9 × 10^20 ATP molecules every minute.
These vital organelles have a surprising past as ancient, free-living bacteria.
